narr: A nearly stationary front draped itself from central Texas northeast through the Ohio River Valley and produced multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms, some with very heavy rainfall. Scattered showers and thunderstorms resulted in several cases of flooding or flash flooding. One to three inches of rain fell across the region with isolated higher amounts before the front passed east on the 25th. Moderate to heavy rainfall quickly inundated ditches and once again flooded roads around the region. Parts of the Ohio and Green Rivers rose above flood stage.
ev: Several roads were closed in Graves County and the city of Mayfield due to flooding. Photos showed several feet of water over a roadway near Wingo. A few miles west of Sedalia, six inches of water was over Highway 339 at Gilpin Road.
Cars were stranded in floodwaters on North 16th Street near Highway 121 in Murray.
About a foot of water was on numerous roadways in the county.
Kentucky Highway 1949 was closed near the Interstate 69 tunnel west of Benton. Kentucky Highway 1462 was closed at the Clarks River bridge on the east side of Benton.
